A license, an hourly wage, and a signed copy of the office policy manual
questions.explanation: The federal test has three parts: licensed, substantially all pay tied to sales or output rather than hours, and a written contract stating the broker won't be treated as an employee for federal tax purposes.

questions.stem: Three brokers at the same firm want to advertise as a team. Which team name complies with Colorado's advertising rules?
choices: The Summit Team
Summit Team Real Estate
The Summit Group Realty
Summit Team, LLC
questions.explanation: Team names can't include words like Realty, Real Estate, or entity endings like LLC that suggest a separate company. Every team ad must also show the firm's name.

questions.stem: A licensed broker is selling a duplex he owns personally, without listing it with any firm. What must he do?
choices: Nothing, because brokers selling their own property are exempt from the license law
Disclose in writing, in the contract, that he holds a Colorado real estate license
Have his employing broker sign the contract as the seller's agent
Tell the buyer orally before showing that he is a licensee
questions.explanation: A broker acting as a principal remains subject to the Commission and must disclose license status in writing; the Commission expects it in the contract. An oral statement isn't enough.

questions.stem: A property manager owns part of the plumbing company she sends to the owners' rentals. What does the Commission expect?
choices: Nothing, as long as the plumbing company charges market rates
Disclosure only if an owner later asks about vendor relationships
She must stop using the company for every property she manages
Written disclosure, ideally early, with an option to opt out
questions.explanation: Brokers have a continuing duty to disclose conflicts in writing. For vendor ties, the Commission recommends disclosure early, such as in the management agreement, and giving the owner an option to opt out.

questions.stem: An associate broker hosts short-term rentals of her own condo and collects guest damage deposits. Her firm's policy manual does not require use of the firm's account. Where must the deposits go?
choices: Her personal checking account, because hosting guests isn't brokerage work
A trust or escrow account she keeps, with a journal and reconciliations
The condo association's reserve account, held there on her guests' behalf
Her firm's operating account, recorded there as her own broker income
questions.explanation: The duty to account for money belonging to others applies whether or not the broker is acting as a broker. Without a firm requirement, she opens her own trust or escrow account, keeps a journal, and reconciles it monthly (a two-way reconciliation).

questions.stem: A buyer and seller sign a contract with an e-signature platform, and the broker emails each party the completed PDF the same day. Has the broker met the duty to provide copies?
choices: No, because only paper copies bearing ink signatures count
No, because an electronic copy must first be notarized
Yes, an e-signed electronic copy counts as a duplicate
Yes, but only if each party later signs a paper original
questions.explanation: Colorado's electronic transactions law gives e-signatures the same effect as ink signatures, and the Commission's definition of a duplicate includes electronic copies with electronic signatures.

questions.stem: A listing expired last month without a sale. Which duty does the former listing broker still owe the seller?
choices: Keep the seller's confidential information confidential
Continue marketing the property until a new firm takes over
Present any offers received for the next six months
Pay the seller's costs of relisting with another firm
questions.explanation: After a brokerage relationship ends, the broker must still account for money or property and keep confidential information confidential unless the party consents in writing, the law requires disclosure, or it becomes public.

questions.stem: During an audit, the Division finds that a firm keeps a few hundred dollars of its own money in its trust account as a cushion. What violation is this?
choices: Commingling
Conversion
Diversion of earnest money
A records-retention violation
questions.explanation: Mixing the firm's own money with money belonging to others is commingling. The exceptions are narrow and must be recorded, such as firm money deposited to cover bank charges; a general cushion isn't one of them.

questions.stem: A property management trust account shows a negative balance on one owner's ledger after the broker paid that owner's repair bill. What does this show?
choices: The broker withdrew an earned management fee too early
The account was not labeled as a trust or escrow account
Other owners' money paid this owner's expense
The bank posted the owner's rent deposit to the wrong account
questions.explanation: A ledger can never go negative. A negative balance means funds belonging to other beneficiaries covered that owner's expense, which is a form of conversion.

questions.stem: A firm is the earnest money holder. The buyer delivers the check on the day after the contract is mutually executed. What is the deposit deadline?
choices: By the end of the next calendar day after receipt
Within 10 business days of mutual execution
Any time before the scheduled closing date
Within 3 business days after receipt
questions.explanation: Earnest money held by a firm must be deposited within 3 business days after receipt or mutual execution of the contract, whichever is later. Here receipt came later, so the clock runs from receipt.

questions.stem: A broker gets a Division notice that he must respond to a complaint by a stated deadline. He believes the complaint is baseless and ignores it. What is the result?
choices: The complaint is dismissed automatically after the deadline
Nothing, unless the complaint is later proven
Failing to respond is itself grounds for discipline
The complainant must refile with the Commission
questions.explanation: A licensee must answer a complaint or audit in writing by the deadline. Failing to do so is grounds for discipline even when the original complaint has no merit.

questions.stem: A broker receives a letter of admonition by certified mail and disagrees with it. What can she do?
choices: Appeal it directly to the Colorado Supreme Court within 60 days
Request formal proceedings in writing within 20 days
File a complaint about the investigator with the governor
Ignore it, because letters of admonition are never acted on
questions.explanation: A licensee may request formal proceedings in writing within 20 days after proven receipt. A timely request vacates the letter and the matter proceeds formally.

questions.stem: A consumer wins a fraud judgment against a Colorado broker but can't collect it. What is true about a state recovery fund?
choices: The Real Estate Recovery Fund pays up to a set cap per transaction
The Commission pays the judgment from fines collected from licensees
The Division pays the judgment from its general operating budget
None exists; Colorado repealed its recovery fund in 2005
questions.explanation: Colorado repealed its Real Estate Recovery Fund in 2005, so no state fund pays these judgments. The consumer must pursue the broker through civil remedies; Commission discipline doesn't compensate the consumer.

questions.stem: A tenant farmer planted corn in the spring. The landlord sold the farm and properly ended the lease in August, before harvest. The tenant did nothing to cause the lease to end. Which statement is most accurate?
choices: The corn became the landlord's real property when planted, so it passes to the new owner and the tenant loses it
The corn is an emblement, and the tenant may generally return to harvest it
The corn passes to the new owner with the deed
The tenant must leave the corn but can sue for its value
questions.explanation: Annual crops planted by human labor (fructus industriales) are emblements, which are personal property. A tenant who didn't cause the lease to end generally may come back and harvest them.

questions.stem: A seller wants to keep the dining-room chandelier, which is wired into the ceiling. The purchase contract lists the chandelier as excluded. Which statement is correct?
choices: The chandelier must stay because it is wired in
The buyer's preference controls because courts favor buyers
The written agreement controls, so the seller may keep it
The chandelier stays because the seller intended it to be permanent
questions.explanation: Under the MARIA tests, a written agreement between the parties overrides the other tests. Without the exclusion, the wired-in chandelier would be a fixture that transfers with the house.

questions.stem: Under the rectangular survey system, where is section 36 located within a township?
choices: Northeast corner
Northwest corner
Center of the township
Southeast corner
questions.explanation: Sections are numbered back and forth starting with section 1 in the northeast corner. Section 6 is in the northwest corner, and section 36 ends up in the southeast corner.

questions.stem: How many acres are in "the N 1/2 of the NW 1/4 and the SE 1/4" of a section?
choices: 240 acres
80 acres
160 acres
40 acres
questions.explanation: "And" means two separate parcels. N 1/2 of the NW 1/4 = 640 ÷ 8 = 80 acres; the SE 1/4 = 640 ÷ 4 = 160 acres; 80 + 160 = 240 acres.

questions.stem: Under the water rights system used in Colorado and many other western states, who generally holds the senior right to water from a river?
choices: The owner whose land borders the river
The first person to put the water to beneficial use
All owners along the river, each sharing reasonable use of the water
The owner of the largest parcel along the river
questions.explanation: Colorado uses prior appropriation: the first to put water to beneficial use holds the senior right, regardless of who owns the riverbank. Sharing reasonable use among bordering owners describes riparian rights.

questions.stem: A Colorado deed conveys a home "to Pat Lee and Sam Ortiz" and says nothing more about how they hold title. How do Pat and Sam own the property?
choices: As joint tenants with right of survivorship
As tenants by the entirety
In severalty
As tenants in common
questions.explanation: Colorado presumes a tenancy in common when property is conveyed to two or more natural persons unless the deed expressly declares a joint tenancy. Severalty means a single owner.

questions.stem: A deed for Colorado property conveys title to a married couple "as tenants by the entirety." What estate does the couple hold?
choices: A joint tenancy
A tenancy by the entirety
A tenancy in common
Community property
questions.explanation: Colorado doesn't recognize tenancy by the entirety. Under C.R.S. 38-31-201, a deed that tries to create one creates a joint tenancy instead. Colorado also isn't a community property state.

questions.stem: A deed conveys land to a town "on condition that" it be used as a park. Years later the town builds offices on the land. What happens?
choices: Title returns to the grantor automatically through a possibility of reverter as soon as the offices are built
The grantor may take action to reclaim the property under a right of reentry
The town keeps title because the condition is unenforceable
Title passes to the state by escheat
questions.explanation: "On condition that" creates a fee simple subject to a condition subsequent. When the condition is broken, the grantor must act to get the property back. Automatic reversion applies to a fee simple determinable ("so long as").

questions.stem: Ann receives a life estate "for the life of Bob." Ann is still living when Bob dies. What happens to Ann's interest?
choices: Ann now owns the property in fee simple
Ann's interest continues until her own death
Ann's estate ends
Ann's heirs receive a remainder
questions.explanation: This is a life estate pur autre vie: the measuring life is Bob's, not Ann's. When Bob dies, Ann's estate ends and the property goes to the reversion or remainder holder.

questions.stem: A tenant's one-year lease ended last month. The tenant is still living in the unit, and the landlord has not agreed to let the tenant stay. What type of tenancy is this?
choices: Month-to-month periodic tenancy
Estate for years
Tenancy at will
Tenancy at sufferance
questions.explanation: A tenancy at sufferance exists when a tenant holds over after the lease ends without the landlord's consent. A tenancy at will requires both parties' agreement and has no set term.

questions.stem: A property is sold at a foreclosure sale. It is subject to a mortgage recorded in 2018, a judgment lien recorded in 2022, and this year's unpaid property taxes. In what order are the liens paid?
choices: Mortgage, judgment, property taxes
Property taxes, mortgage, judgment
Judgment, mortgage, property taxes
Property taxes, judgment, mortgage
questions.explanation: Property tax liens generally take priority over all other liens regardless of recording date. The remaining liens rank by recording date: first in time, first in right.

questions.stem: An electric utility holds a recorded right to run power lines across a farm. No neighboring parcel benefits from the right. What type of interest does the utility hold?
choices: A commercial easement in gross
An easement appurtenant benefiting the farm
A license
An encroachment
questions.explanation: An easement in gross has a servient tenement but no dominant tenement; it benefits a person or company. Commercial easements in gross such as utility lines are usually transferable. A license is personal, revocable permission and isn't an interest in land.

questions.stem: Lot A has a recorded easement for a driveway across Lot B. The owner of Lot A then buys Lot B. What happens to the easement?
choices: It continues because recorded easements can't end
It becomes a license
It ends by merger
It becomes a prescriptive easement
questions.explanation: When one person comes to own both the dominant and servient parcels, the easement ends by merger, because no one needs an easement over their own land.

questions.stem: A church wants to build in a residential zone. The zoning ordinance lists churches as allowed in that zone if parking and landscaping requirements are met. What does the church need?
choices: A variance based on hardship
A nonconforming use
Spot zoning
A conditional use permit
questions.explanation: A conditional use permit allows a use the ordinance lists as permitted if conditions are met, because it serves the community. A variance relieves an owner from strict physical standards because of a property-related hardship.

questions.stem: A new airport flight path runs low over a homeowner's property, sharply reducing its value. The government has not started any condemnation proceeding. What can the homeowner file?
choices: An inverse condemnation suit
A request for a variance
A quiet title action against the airport
A petition for escheat
questions.explanation: Inverse condemnation is a lawsuit an owner brings when government action has effectively taken or damaged property without a formal condemnation.

questions.stem: A city council rezones a single lot in a residential neighborhood to commercial so its owner can open a store. The change benefits only that owner and conflicts with the comprehensive plan. This is
choices: downzoning
cumulative zoning
spot zoning
a buffer zone
questions.explanation: Spot zoning rezones a single parcel to benefit one owner in a way that conflicts with the comprehensive plan, and it is often struck down. Downzoning is a change to a less intense use.

questions.stem: A bank is selling a home it acquired through foreclosure. It is willing to warrant title only against defects that arose while the bank owned the property. Which deed will it most likely use?
choices: General warranty deed
Special warranty deed
Quitclaim deed
Personal representative's deed
questions.explanation: A special warranty deed warrants only against defects arising during the grantor's ownership and is typical for lenders selling REO property. A general warranty deed covers defects at any time, and a quitclaim gives no warranties at all.

questions.stem: In a deed of trust, what is the borrower called?
choices: Beneficiary
Trustee
Trustor
Mortgagee
questions.explanation: A deed of trust has three parties: the trustor (borrower), the beneficiary (lender) and the trustee. A mortgagee is the lender under a mortgage.

questions.stem: A buyer takes title "subject to" the seller's existing loan and makes the payments. The buyer later defaults. Who is personally liable on the loan?
choices: The seller
The buyer
Both the buyer and the seller equally
Neither, because the lender can only foreclose
questions.explanation: When a buyer takes subject to a loan, the buyer is not personally liable and the seller remains liable. In an assumption, the buyer becomes personally liable and the seller stays secondarily liable unless a novation releases them.

questions.stem: Which clause requires the lender to release its lien once the borrower pays the debt in full?
choices: Acceleration clause
Release clause
Subordination clause
Defeasance clause
questions.explanation: The defeasance clause requires the lender to release the lien when the debt is paid. A release clause frees individual parcels from a blanket loan as they are sold.

questions.stem: An applicant has gross monthly income of $6,000, a proposed PITI payment of $1,500, and other monthly debts of $600. What is the total debt (back-end) ratio?
questions.explanation: Total debt ratio = (housing payment + other monthly debts) ÷ gross monthly income = ($1,500 + $600) ÷ $6,000 = 35%. The housing (front-end) ratio would be $1,500 ÷ $6,000 = 25%.

questions.stem: An ARM's current rate is 4.00%. At the next adjustment, the index is 3.50% and the margin is 2.25%. The periodic cap is 1%. What is the new rate?
questions.explanation: The fully indexed rate would be 3.50% + 2.25% = 5.75%, but the 1% periodic cap limits the increase to 4.00% + 1% = 5.00%.

questions.stem: A borrower's ARM has a payment cap that keeps monthly payments below the interest due. What happens to the unpaid interest?
choices: It is forgiven by the lender
It is added to the loan balance
It is due as a lump sum at the next adjustment
It is paid by the mortgage insurer
questions.explanation: This is negative amortization: unpaid interest is added to the balance, so the borrower owes more over time.

questions.stem: Which loan is designed for older homeowners with substantial equity, pays money to the owner, and has a balance that grows until the owner sells, moves out permanently or dies?
choices: Reverse mortgage
Home equity line of credit
Bridge loan
Wraparound mortgage
questions.explanation: In a reverse mortgage, the lender pays the owner and the balance grows; it is repaid when the borrower sells, moves out permanently or dies. A HELOC is a revolving line the borrower draws on and repays.

questions.stem: A conventional loan exceeds the maximum loan size that Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will buy. What is it called?
choices: A conforming loan
A package loan
A jumbo loan
An open-end loan
questions.explanation: A jumbo loan is a nonconforming loan that exceeds the conforming loan limit. Conforming loans meet Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac guidelines, including the maximum loan size.

questions.stem: A brokerage owns part of a title company and refers its buyers there. Under RESPA, which condition must be met?
choices: The buyers must be required to use the affiliated title company
The brokerage must receive a fee for each referral
The buyers must get a written disclosure of the affiliated relationship
The title company must charge buyers less than competing title companies in the area
questions.explanation: An affiliated business arrangement is allowed only if the consumer receives a written disclosure, isn't required to use the affiliate, and the only thing of value received is a return on ownership interest, not a per-referral fee.

questions.stem: Which payment between settlement service providers is permitted under RESPA on a federally related loan?
choices: A cooperative commission split from the listing firm to the buyer's firm
A lender's $100 gift card to a broker for each referred buyer
An inspector's payment to a broker for steering clients
A title company's payment to a broker for referrals, when the buyer pays nothing extra
questions.explanation: Cooperative commission splits between brokers pay for real brokerage services and are allowed. Payments for referring settlement business are prohibited kickbacks, even when the consumer pays nothing extra.

questions.stem: A homeowner refinances the loan on her principal residence with a different lender. Under the Truth in Lending Act, what right does she generally have?
choices: A 30-day right to cancel any home loan
A three-business-day right of rescission
A three-business-day right of rescission that covers home-equity lines but not refinances
No right of rescission because the loan is secured by real property
questions.explanation: TILA gives a three-business-day right of rescission on certain refinances and home-equity loans secured by a principal residence. It does not apply to a loan used to buy the home, so being secured by real property doesn't remove the right.

questions.stem: Why is a loan's annual percentage rate (APR) usually higher than its note rate?
choices: The APR includes property taxes and homeowners insurance
The APR is calculated on the purchase price rather than the loan amount
The APR assumes the rate will rise to its lifetime cap over the life of the loan
The APR includes certain finance charges, such as points, as well as interest
questions.explanation: Under TILA and Regulation Z, the APR expresses interest plus certain finance charges, such as points and some fees, as a yearly rate. That's why it is usually higher than the note rate.

questions.stem: A lender receives a consumer's completed loan application, including all six required items, on a Monday. Under TRID, the Loan Estimate must be delivered or mailed
choices: no later than the third business day after the application is received
within 30 days of the application
at least three business days before the borrower signs the loan documents at closing
on the day the application is received
questions.explanation: The creditor must deliver or mail the Loan Estimate no later than the third business day after receiving the application. The three-days-before-consummation rule applies to receiving the Closing Disclosure.

questions.stem: Two days after a borrower receives the Closing Disclosure, the loan changes from a fixed-rate loan to an adjustable-rate loan. What is required?
choices: Only a corrected Closing Disclosure at or before closing, with no new waiting period
A new Loan Estimate, with no waiting period
A new Closing Disclosure and a new three-business-day waiting period
Nothing, if the borrower agrees verbally
questions.explanation: Only three changes restart the three-day clock: the APR becomes inaccurate beyond tolerance, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added. A switch from fixed to adjustable is a product change.

questions.stem: A lender denies a loan because the applicant's income comes from public assistance. Which law does this violate?
choices: The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act
The Equal Credit Opportunity Act
The Truth in Lending Act
TRID
questions.explanation: ECOA bars credit discrimination based on receipt of public assistance income, as well as marital status and age, which the federal Fair Housing Act does not list.

questions.stem: A buyer purchases a home for $300,000 with a 90% loan. Buyer closing costs are $5,000, the lender charges 1 point, the buyer deposited $8,000 in earnest money, and the buyer receives a $900 tax proration credit. How much cash does the buyer need at closing?
questions.explanation: Loan = $270,000, so the down payment is $30,000. Add costs and the point ($2,700): $37,700. Subtract earnest money and the proration credit: $37,700 − $8,000 − $900 = $28,800.

questions.stem: A $250,000 loan at 6% interest for 30 years has a monthly principal-and-interest payment of $1,498.88. How much of the first payment goes to principal?
A builder has a $600,000 construction loan, and $200,000 has been disbursed in draws so far. On what amount does the builder usually pay interest?
choices: The full $600,000 loan amount
The $400,000 not yet disbursed
Nothing until construction is complete
The $200,000 drawn so far
questions.explanation: With a construction loan, the borrower usually pays interest only on the amount drawn so far, not on the full loan.

questions.stem: Which body sets the minimum education, experience and exam requirements for real property appraisers?
choices: The Appraisal Standards Board
The Appraiser Qualifications Board
ARELLO
The Colorado Real Estate Commission
questions.explanation: The Appraiser Qualifications Board of The Appraisal Foundation sets minimum qualification criteria; states license appraisers using criteria at least that strict. The Appraisal Standards Board writes USPAP.

questions.stem: Which appraiser credential level may work only under the supervision of a certified appraiser?
choices: Trainee
Licensed residential
Certified residential
Certified general
questions.explanation: A trainee works only under a certified appraiser's supervision. The licensed, certified residential and certified general levels can appraise progressively more complex property on their own.

questions.stem: A buyer and a seller both believed the sale included a vacant parcel across the road. After signing, they learn the parcel was never part of the seller's property. The contract is most likely
choices: fully enforceable, because a mistake is never a defense to a signed contract
void or voidable, because both parties were mistaken about a material fact
voidable only by the seller, because the seller owned the property being sold
unenforceable under the Statute of Frauds, because the parcel was described in writing
questions.explanation: A mutual mistake about a material fact can make a contract void or voidable. A unilateral mistake, or a mistake about value or the law, usually isn't a defense, but here both parties shared the mistake.

questions.stem: A buyer promises to pay $400,000 and the seller promises to convey the house at closing. Classified by who is bound, this purchase contract is
choices: unilateral, because only the buyer has to come up with money
implied, because it is created by the parties' conduct
bilateral
voidable by either party until closing
questions.explanation: A bilateral contract is a promise for a promise, so both parties are obligated. A unilateral contract is a promise for an act (like an option), where only one party is bound.

questions.stem: A buyer discovers the seller lied about a material fact to get the buyer to sign. The buyer wants to cancel the contract and get the earnest money deposit back. Which remedy fits?
choices: Rescission
Specific performance
Liquidated damages
Acceptance of breach
questions.explanation: Rescission cancels the contract and puts the parties back where they started, with deposits returned; it's the typical remedy for a contract induced by fraud or mutual mistake. Specific performance would force the sale to go through, the opposite of what the buyer wants.

questions.stem: A tenant has a one-year lease with fixed start and end dates. Four months in, the owner sells the building. What happens to the lease?
choices: It ends automatically when the deed is recorded
The new owner takes title subject to the existing lease
It converts to a tenancy at will that either party can end
It becomes a periodic tenancy that the new owner can end on notice
questions.explanation: A sale doesn't end an estate for years; the buyer takes the property subject to existing leases. The tenant keeps possession through the lease's end date.

questions.stem: A tenant signs a lease that gives her the right, but not the obligation, to buy the home at a set price during the term. This arrangement is a
choices: lease-purchase
graduated lease
ground lease
lease option
questions.explanation: A lease option is a lease plus an option to buy: the tenant may buy but isn't required to. In a lease-purchase, the tenant agrees to buy, so both sides are obligated to complete the sale.

questions.stem: An owner buys an NFIP flood insurance policy on his own; no loan is being made, increased, extended or renewed. When does coverage generally begin?
choices: Immediately, on the day the premium is paid
After the next FEMA flood map update
After a 30-day waiting period
Only once the home is placed in a special flood hazard area
questions.explanation: NFIP policies generally have a 30-day waiting period. The exception is a policy bought in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan, which doesn't apply here. Owners outside mapped high-risk zones can still buy flood coverage.

questions.stem: A listing broker receives a second offer on the seller's home while the seller is reviewing the first one. Which fiduciary duty requires the broker to tell the seller about it?
choices: Disclosure
Confidentiality
Obedience
Accounting
questions.explanation: The duty of disclosure requires the broker to tell the client everything material, including other offers. Confidentiality works the other way: it protects the client's private information from others.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker recommends a roofing contractor to repair the roof after closing. The contractor pays the broker a fee for every client referred. What is the broker's obligation?
choices: Nothing, because the contractor is not a party to the real estate transaction
Disclose the fee in writing before the client relies on the recommendation
Mention the fee to the client verbally at any point before the closing appointment
Nothing, as long as the contractor's prices are in line with other local contractors
questions.explanation: A broker must disclose any personal interest, including a referral fee from a vendor they recommend, in writing before the client relies on it. A verbal mention, or a fair price, doesn't cure it; an undisclosed payment is a secret profit that violates the duty of loyalty.

questions.stem: Two competing brokers agree that one will take listings only on the west side of town and the other only on the east side. This antitrust violation is
choices: a tie-in arrangement
price fixing
a group boycott
market allocation
questions.explanation: Market allocation is competitors dividing up territory, customers, price ranges or property types. Price fixing concerns agreed rates, a group boycott targets a competitor, and a tie-in conditions one product on buying another.

questions.stem: A licensee paid entirely by commission wants to be treated as a statutory nonemployee for federal tax purposes. Besides being licensed and paid based on sales output, what else is required?
choices: A written agreement stating she won't be treated as an employee for federal tax purposes
At least two years of continuous affiliation with the same employing broker
An agreement that the employing broker will stop supervising her work
Proof that she pays for her own errors and omissions coverage
questions.explanation: The IRS treats a licensed agent as a statutory nonemployee when she is licensed, substantially all pay is based on sales output, and a written agreement says she won't be treated as an employee for federal tax purposes. License law still requires the employing broker to supervise her either way.

questions.stem: In most states, which task may a broker's unlicensed assistant perform?
choices: Hold an open house alone on a weekend
Schedule showing appointments for the broker
Discuss price and terms with a buyer who calls
Show a listing to a buyer when the broker is busy
questions.explanation: Unlicensed assistants may do clerical and administrative work such as scheduling, data entry and ordering reports. Showing property, negotiating, discussing terms and holding open houses alone are licensed activities.

questions.stem: A property manager sets aside a plan for replacing the roof and parking lot over the next several years. This is part of the
choices: operating budget
stabilized budget
capital budget
management agreement
questions.explanation: A capital budget plans for big-ticket replacements and improvements such as a roof, HVAC or parking lot. An operating budget projects the year's income and ordinary expenses; a stabilized budget averages expenses over several years.

questions.stem: A tenant is two months behind on rent. The landlord changes the locks while the tenant is at work. This is
choices: a lawful actual eviction, because the tenant breached the lease
generally illegal self-help; the landlord should use the court eviction process
a constructive eviction, which a landlord may use once rent is two months late
permitted if the landlord gives notice of the lock change the same day
questions.explanation: Actual eviction means removing the tenant through a court process after a breach. Self-help, such as changing locks or shutting off utilities, is generally illegal. Constructive eviction is a tenant's claim when the landlord makes the premises unusable, not a landlord remedy.

questions.stem: After several injuries, the owner of an apartment complex closes the swimming pool permanently. Which risk management strategy is this?
choices: Transfer
Control
Retain
Avoid
questions.explanation: Avoiding risk means removing the activity that creates it, such as closing the pool. Control reduces the chance or size of a loss (better lighting, handrails), transfer shifts it (insurance), and retain accepts it.

questions.stem: Under the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA), when does the act apply to a real estate transaction?
choices: Only when the parties have agreed to deal electronically, which can be shown by their conduct
In every transaction, whether or not the parties want electronic records
Only when the documents are notarized by an electronic notary
Only to commercial transactions, not consumer home sales
questions.explanation: UETA applies only when the parties agree to conduct the transaction electronically, and that agreement can be shown by conduct. Neither UETA nor E-SIGN forces anyone to use electronic records.

questions.stem: Dana is the salaried on-site manager of an apartment building and shows vacant units and takes rental applications as part of her customary duties. She has no real estate license. Which statement is correct?
choices: Dana needs a license because showing units and taking applications are leasing activities
Dana is exempt only if she shows fewer than ten units in a calendar year
Dana is exempt as a salaried on-site manager performing customary duties
Dana must be supervised by an employing broker but does not need her own license
questions.explanation: Colorado exempts a salaried on-site manager of an apartment building or condominium who is doing customary duties. There is no unit-count limit in the exemption.

questions.stem: A broker wants to qualify as an employing broker so she can hire other brokers. Which requirement applies?
choices: Two years of active practice in the prior five years, an experience point requirement, and a 24-hour Brokerage Administration course
Two years of Active licensure as an associate broker, with no further coursework
One year of Active licensure and passing the state portion of the exam a second time
Five years as an independent broker and a written recommendation from her current employing broker
questions.explanation: An employing broker needs two years of active practice in the prior five years, must meet an experience point requirement, and must complete a 24-hour Brokerage Administration course. Two years of Active licensure alone qualifies a broker only for independent status.

questions.stem: A newly approved broker applicant receives the Commission's notice but does not provide proof of E&O insurance or the name of an employing broker within 30 days. What happens?
choices: The application is denied and the applicant must retake the exam
The license is issued Active for 90 days while coverage is obtained
The applicant must restart the 168-hour pre-licensing education
The license is issued Inactive
questions.explanation: If proof of E&O coverage or an employing broker isn't provided within 30 days of the Commission's notice, the license is issued Inactive. The broker can't do licensed work until the license is Active.

questions.stem: The only employing broker of a small Colorado brokerage firm suddenly leaves. What relief can the Division director provide while the firm finds a replacement?
choices: A temporary license for up to 90 days, with one extension of up to 90 days for good cause
Permission for the senior associate broker to act as employing broker indefinitely
A one-year waiver of supervision requirements for all associates
Nothing; the firm must stop all brokerage activity until the Commission approves a successor
questions.explanation: The Division director can issue a temporary license for up to 90 days, with one extension of up to 90 days for good cause, while the firm finds a new employing broker.

questions.stem: How many hours of approved pre-licensing education must a Colorado broker applicant complete (unless the applicant holds a college degree with a real estate major)?
choices: 48 hours
72 hours
168 hours
120 hours
questions.explanation: Colorado requires 168 hours: 48 hours of real estate law and practice, 48 hours of Colorado contracts and regulations, and 72 hours of trust accounts, closings, legal issues, and practical applications. 48 and 72 are only components of the total.

questions.stem: Which Colorado broker must maintain a place of business in Colorado?
choices: An associate broker who works from home for a Denver firm
An inactive broker who lives in Colorado
An independent broker who lives in Colorado
An associate broker whose employing broker has several branch offices
questions.explanation: Independent and employing brokers who live in Colorado must maintain a Colorado place of business. Associate brokers and inactive brokers are exempt.

questions.stem: A broker's first Colorado license is issued on October 15, 2026. When does it expire?
choices: October 15, 2027
December 31, 2026
December 31, 2029
October 15, 2029
questions.explanation: A new license expires at midnight on December 31 of the year it was issued, regardless of the issue date. After that, licenses run on three-year calendar cycles.

questions.stem: How many hours of continuing education must an active Colorado broker complete in each three-year license cycle?
choices: 12 hours, all from the Annual Commission Update
24 hours, including the 4-hour Annual Commission Update each year
36 hours, including 12 hours of contracts
24 hours of electives chosen by the broker, with no required courses
questions.explanation: Colorado requires 24 CE hours per three-year cycle. Twelve come from the 4-hour Annual Commission Update taken every year, and the other 12 are Commission-approved electives.

questions.stem: An active broker skipped the Annual Commission Update in the first year of her cycle and wants to take two versions in year two to catch up. What is the rule?
choices: She may take both versions in year two as long as she finishes before renewal
She may substitute 4 extra elective hours for the missed update course
She can't make up the missed course and must use an alternative such as the 24-hour Broker Reactivation course
She is excused because the update course is required only in the final year of the cycle
questions.explanation: A missed year's Annual Commission Update can't be made up later. A broker who falls short must use an alternative, such as a 24-hour Broker Reactivation course, passing the state exam, or completing 72 hours of contracts/regulations and closings coursework.

questions.stem: A broker's license expired on December 31, and he applies to reinstate it six months later. What must he pay?
choices: Only the regular renewal fee
The renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee equal to half the renewal fee
The renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee equal to the full renewal fee
Nothing until he retakes the exam as a new applicant
questions.explanation: More than 31 days but no more than one year after expiration, reinstatement costs the renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee of half the renewal fee. The full-fee reinstatement charge applies after one year, up to three years.

questions.stem: Marco placed his license on inactive status after leaving his firm. Which statement about his inactive license is correct?
choices: He must keep carrying E&O insurance while inactive
He no longer needs to renew the license or pay renewal fees
He may continue to show property as long as he does not write contracts
His former employing broker may still pay him commissions earned while he was Active
questions.explanation: An inactive broker can still be paid by a former employing broker for commissions earned while Active. Inactive brokers must still renew and pay fees, don't need E&O, and can't do anything that requires a license.

questions.stem: A broker enters a no contest plea to a criminal charge. What must the broker do?
choices: Give the Commission written notice within 30 calendar days
Report it at the next license renewal
Notify the Commission only if the plea results in a conviction
Notify the employing broker, who reports it to the Commission annually
questions.explanation: A broker must give the Commission written notice within 30 calendar days of a conviction or a guilty or no contest plea; deferred judgments count too. Waiting for renewal or for a conviction is too late.

questions.stem: A broker is shopping for an independent E&O policy instead of the Division's group plan. Which policy meets Colorado's minimum terms for individual coverage?
choices: $50,000 per claim, $150,000 aggregate, $500 deductible
$100,000 per claim, $300,000 aggregate, $1,000 deductible
$100,000 per claim, $300,000 aggregate, $2,500 deductible
$100,000 per claim, $200,000 aggregate, $1,000 deductible
questions.explanation: Individual coverage must be at least $100,000 per claim and $300,000 annual aggregate, with a deductible of no more than $1,000 per occurrence. A $2,500 deductible is too high, and a $200,000 aggregate is too low.

questions.stem: An active broker forgets to pay his E&O premium and the coverage lapses. What happens to his license?
choices: It stays Active for a 30-day grace period
It is automatically revoked
It goes Inactive immediately
It expires at the end of the current renewal cycle
questions.explanation: If E&O coverage lapses, or the broker fails to certify continuing coverage, the license goes Inactive immediately. Doing brokerage while uninsured is acting on an inactive license.

questions.stem: A broker's license has been inactive for four years and she wants to reactivate it. Which option satisfies the education or testing requirement?
choices: Completing only the current year's Annual Commission Update
Passing the state portion of the exam
Completing 12 hours of elective CE
Showing proof of E&O coverage alone
questions.explanation: When a license has been inactive for more than three years, reactivation requires passing the state exam or completing 72 hours of coursework (48 hours of contracts and regulations plus 24 hours of closings).

questions.stem: A seller asks a Colorado broker to take a net listing at $400,000, with the broker keeping anything above that. Which statement best reflects Colorado's position?
choices: Net listings are illegal in Colorado, and the broker would lose the license for taking one
Net listings are allowed only on the Commission-approved net listing form
They aren't expressly prohibited but are discouraged, mainly because of secret-profit risk
Net listings are permitted only for commercial property
questions.explanation: Colorado's statute and current Commission rules don't expressly prohibit net listings, but the Commission discourages them. There is no Commission-approved net listing form, and a broker who uses one to take an undisclosed profit can be disciplined for secret compensation.

questions.stem: After a residential sale, a firm believes the seller still owes part of its commission. Before filing a lien or lis pendens against the property, the firm must:
choices: Obtain a court judgment
File a complaint with the Commission so it can decide the dispute
Give the seller 10 days' written notice
Get the buyer's written consent
questions.explanation: In residential deals, a firm can't file a lien or lis pendens or otherwise cloud title to collect a disputed commission without first getting a court judgment. The Commission doesn't decide money disputes; those go to court or arbitration.

questions.stem: A sale closed on August 15, 2026. Under Colorado's record retention rule, until at least what date must the broker keep the transaction file?
choices: August 15, 2029
August 15, 2030
August 15, 2031
December 31, 2029
questions.explanation: Required records must be kept for four years, starting from the date the transaction closed. Three- and five-year periods are common distractors.

questions.stem: A firm stores all its transaction files electronically. During a Commission audit, the server crashes and the broker can't retrieve the files. Which statement is correct?
choices: The broker is excused until the system is repaired, however long that takes
The broker may substitute a written summary of each transaction
Electronic storage is not allowed for trust account records, so the firm is already in violation
A technical problem is not an excuse; the broker must still produce the records
questions.explanation: Records may be kept electronically, but they must stay retrievable and legibly printable for four years, and a technical problem with the storage system is not an excuse for failing to produce them. Trust account records may also be kept electronically.

questions.stem: Who can require a broker to produce electronic or printed copies of a transaction's required records?
choices: Only the Commission
The Commission or any principal party to the transaction
Only the broker's employing broker
Any member of the public
questions.explanation: Electronic or printed copies must be produced when the Commission or any principal party to the transaction asks.

questions.stem: A broker receives notice of a complaint that she is sure has no merit, so she ignores the Commission's response deadline. What is the likely result?
choices: Nothing, because the complaint will be dismissed anyway
The complaint is automatically transferred to small claims court
She can face discipline for failing to respond on time, even if the complaint lacks merit
Her employing broker must answer for her, and she has no further obligation
questions.explanation: A broker notified of a complaint or audit must respond in writing by the Commission's deadline, addressing each allegation and including the complete transaction file. Failing to respond on time is itself grounds for discipline, even if the complaint has no merit.

questions.stem: After closing, which item does the Commission NOT require a broker to keep in the transaction file?
choices: The buyer's loan application
The signed contract to buy and sell
The brokerage disclosure
The closing statement
questions.explanation: After closing, the Commission doesn't require you to keep copies of loan applications, title commitments, existing public records, lender-required disclosures, or affirmations from independent closing entities. Contracts, brokerage disclosures, and closing statements are on the Transaction File Checklist.

questions.stem: Which record must a firm keep for each beneficiary of a trust account, showing receipts and disbursements with no negative balance?
choices: The journal
The deposit agreement
The accounting control policy
The ledger
questions.explanation: A ledger is kept for each beneficiary, shows the same details as the journal, and may never have a negative balance. The journal is a single chronological record of all receipts and disbursements for the account.

questions.stem: An associate broker moves from Firm A to Firm B. Who is responsible for keeping the transaction files from his deals at Firm A?
choices: Only Firm A, because listings belong to the firm
Only the Commission, which takes custody of files when a broker transfers
The broker himself remains responsible for keeping those files
No one, because files may be destroyed once a broker transfers
questions.explanation: A broker stays responsible for keeping their transaction files even after moving to a new brokerage. Each broker and brokerage keeps a transaction file for every transaction.

questions.stem: A broker exchanged dozens of emails and texts with a buyer during a transaction. Under Division guidance, which statement is correct?
choices: They must be printed and kept for four years
Keeping them is recommended but not required
They must be deleted after closing to protect privacy
They must be sent to the Commission at closing
questions.explanation: The Division recommends, but does not require, keeping related emails and texts. The required file contents are listed on the Commission's Transaction File Checklist, and a firm may require more.

questions.stem: During negotiation, the seller tells the listing broker to remove a printed paragraph from a Commission-approved form. How should the broker show the deletion?
choices: Erase or white out the paragraph so the final form looks clean
Retype the form without the paragraph in the same font
Strike through the text so it can still be read
Leave the text in place and explain the change to the parties in an email
questions.explanation: Printed text is deleted only because of negotiation or a party's instruction, and it is struck through so it remains legible. It is never silently erased or retyped away.

questions.stem: A broker inserts an attorney-drafted clause into the Additional Provisions of a contract. Under Commission rules, how long must the broker keep a copy of that clause, with the attorney's name?
choices: 4 years from its last use
1 year from closing
3 years from its first use
For as long as the broker holds a license
questions.explanation: Commission rules require the broker to keep an attorney-drafted clause, with the attorney's name, for 4 years from its last use and to provide it to the Commission on request.

questions.stem: The buyer's lender approves the loan, but the interest rate offered is higher than the buyer is willing to accept. Under the Colorado residential contract, which deadline should the buyer use to terminate?
choices: New Loan Availability Deadline
Appraisal Objection Deadline
New Loan Terms Deadline
New Loan Application Deadline
questions.explanation: Unsatisfactory loan terms such as the rate are handled by the New Loan Terms Deadline, in the buyer's sole discretion. The New Loan Availability Deadline is for an unsatisfactory underwriting result and can't be used for problems with the loan terms.

questions.stem: A buyer makes an offer. The seller responds with a Counterproposal, which the buyer lets expire. The seller now wants to sign the buyer's original offer. What is the result?
choices: The original offer revives automatically once the counterproposal expires
The seller can't accept it, because the counterproposal rejected the original offer
The seller can accept it by signing before the original Acceptance Deadline
The seller can accept it by sending an Agreement to Amend/Extend
questions.explanation: Under general contract law, a counteroffer rejects the original offer, so that offer is gone. The parties would need a new offer or counterproposal.

questions.stem: A contract terminated when the parties failed to sign an Inspection Resolution by the Inspection Resolution Deadline. Two days later, both parties want the deal back on. Which Commission form fits?
choices: Agreement to Amend/Extend Contract
Inspection Objection Notice
Earnest Money Release
Agreement to Revive Contract
questions.explanation: A terminated contract can't be amended, because nothing is left to amend. The Agreement to Revive Contract brings it back: the parties state the termination date, ratify the contract and set new deadlines.

questions.stem: A seller already under contract receives a better offer and wants to accept it. How should the second contract be structured to avoid two binding contracts?
choices: As a backup offer that depends on the first contract terminating
As a counterproposal that supersedes the first contract
As an Agreement to Amend/Extend the first contract with the new buyer's terms
As a new contract signed first, with a Notice to Terminate sent to the first buyer afterward
questions.explanation: A seller who accepts a second offer should make it a backup offer contingent on the first contract terminating. Otherwise the seller risks being bound to two contracts.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker has submitted an offer, but the listing broker won't respond to calls or emails. What should the buyer's broker do first?
choices: Deliver the offer directly to the seller
File a complaint with the Real Estate Commission
Contact the listing broker's employing broker
Have the buyer withdraw the offer and resubmit it later
questions.explanation: The buyer's broker goes to the listing broker's employing broker first. Only if that fails does the buyer's broker go to the seller directly.

questions.stem: A seller signs the Exclusive Right-to-Sell Listing Contract but checks neither the seller agency box nor the transaction-brokerage box. What is the broker's relationship with the seller?
choices: Seller's agent
Transaction-broker
Dual agent for the seller and any buyer
No brokerage relationship until a box is checked
questions.explanation: If neither relationship box is checked in the listing contract, the broker is a transaction-broker.

questions.stem: An HOA board wants to fine an owner for leaving trash cans out. The association has no written fine policy. Under CCIOA, what is the board's position?
choices: It may fine the owner if the rules and regulations prohibit the conduct
It may fine the owner after a majority vote of the owners
It may fine the owner only up to six months of regular assessments
It can't fine the owner without a written policy providing notice and a hearing
questions.explanation: An HOA can't fine an owner without a written fine policy that gives notice and an opportunity to be heard. Associations must adopt written governance policies, including a covenant-enforcement policy.

questions.stem: An owner is fully paid up on assessments but owes the HOA $3,000 in fines, late charges and interest. Can the association foreclose its CCIOA lien based on that balance?
choices: Yes, once the balance equals six months of assessments
No, those items alone can't be the basis of a CCIOA foreclosure
Yes, if the board records a vote authorizing the foreclosure
No, because fines can't be secured by the HOA lien at all
questions.explanation: Fines, fees, late charges and interest can be secured by the lien, but they can't by themselves be the basis of a CCIOA foreclosure. Foreclosure requires a lien balance of at least six months of common-expense assessments plus a recorded board vote.

questions.stem: In general, the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act applies to common interest communities created:
choices: on or after July 1, 1992
before January 1, 1970
only after its 2015 amendments
on or after January 1, 2000
questions.explanation: CCIOA applies to communities created on or after July 1, 1992, with limited exceptions. Older communities are reached only by the specific sections listed in C.R.S. 38-33.3-117.

questions.stem: A buyer pays all cash for a Colorado home, so there is no lender and no federal Closing Disclosure. What closing document must the broker still make sure the buyer receives?
choices: A loan estimate prepared by the title company
An accurate closing statement signed by the broker
No closing document, because a cash sale has no federal disclosure
A Closing Disclosure prepared by the listing broker
questions.explanation: A cash sale has no Closing Disclosure, but every transaction, cash or financed, still needs a closing statement. The broker must see that the consumer receives an accurate, complete closing statement signed by the broker.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Real Property Transfer Declaration (TD-1000) filed with a Colorado deed?
choices: It calculates the documentary fee owed to the state
It notifies the county treasurer that taxes have been paid
It informs the assessor of the sale price
It gives public notice of the buyer's ownership
questions.explanation: The TD-1000 is filed with the deed so the assessor learns the sale price. The clerk sends it to the assessor, and it is not a public record.

questions.stem: A buyer wants protection against unrecorded mechanics' liens and matters a survey would show. What should the buyer ask for under the Colorado contract?
choices: Owner's extended coverage
A lender's title policy
A certificate of taxes due
A standard owner's policy
questions.explanation: Owner's extended coverage (OEC) removes the standard exceptions, such as unrecorded mechanics' liens and survey matters. The contract states whether OEC is provided and who pays the extra premium.

questions.stem: Which person can manage rental property for compensation in Colorado WITHOUT a real estate broker's license?
choices: An independent manager who leases homes for several owners for a percentage of rents
A regularly salaried on-site manager of an apartment building doing customary duties
A person who lists a neighbor's condo for rent online for a flat fee
An employee of an investor who leases the investor's scattered single-family homes for a fee
questions.explanation: The exception is narrow: a regularly salaried employee of the owner of an apartment building or condominium units who acts as the on-site manager, doing only customary on-site duties. Leasing for others for compensation otherwise requires a license, even as the owner's employee.

questions.stem: A property management firm collects a tenant's rent on Monday. Within what time must the firm deposit it into its rent trust account?
choices: One business day
Three business days
Ten calendar days
Five business days
questions.explanation: Property management funds must be deposited within five business days after receipt (or after the lease is signed, if later). The three-business-day deadline applies to other trust money such as earnest money.

questions.stem: A landlord keeps part of a tenant's security deposit for carpet damage but never sends a written statement listing the reasons. What is the consequence under Colorado law?
choices: The landlord forfeits the right to keep any part of the deposit
The landlord may keep the amount if the damage is documented with photos
The landlord must pay a $500 penalty but may keep the deduction
The tenant must sue within 7 days or the deduction stands
questions.explanation: A landlord who fails to deliver the written statement of reasons within the deadline forfeits the right to keep any part of the deposit. The 7-day figure is the notice a tenant gives before suing for willful retention, not a deadline to sue.

questions.stem: A tenant gives proper written notice of a condition that materially interferes with life, health or safety. Under Colorado's warranty of habitability, when must the landlord begin fixing it?
choices: Within 96 hours
Within 24 hours
Within 10 days
Within 30 days
questions.explanation: For a condition that materially interferes with life, health or safety, the landlord must respond within 24 hours and begin remedial action within 24 hours. The 96-hour window is for other conditions that make the unit uninhabitable.

questions.stem: A tenant is two months behind on rent. The landlord changes the locks while the tenant is at work, without a court order. What is the landlord's position under Colorado law?
choices: The lockout is lawful because the rent is more than 30 days late
The lockout is lawful if a 10-day demand was served first
It's unlawful, and the tenant can recover damages and attorney fees
It's unlawful only if the lease bans lockouts
questions.explanation: Removing or locking out a tenant without court process is unlawful. The tenant can recover actual damages plus the greater of three months' rent or $5,000, and attorney fees, no matter how much rent is owed.

questions.stem: A covered residential tenant has lived in a Colorado apartment for two years and has followed the lease. The landlord simply prefers a new tenant and wants to decline to renew. Under Colorado's for-cause eviction law, what is the general rule?
choices: The landlord may decline with 10 days' written notice
The landlord may decline at the end of any lease term
The landlord generally needs cause or a qualifying no-fault reason
The landlord may decline only if rent rises above market
questions.explanation: Colorado's 2024 for-cause law generally requires a landlord to have cause, or a qualifying no-fault reason with longer written notice, to refuse to renew a covered tenant who has lived in the unit 12 months or more. The details have since been amended, but the principle holds: simply preferring a new tenant isn't a reason.

questions.stem: A buyer is acquiring shares in a mutual ditch company along with a farm. How do those shares transfer?
choices: By a recorded warranty deed, like the land
By decree of the water court
By the water right passing automatically with the land
By stock assignment and a new company certificate
questions.explanation: Mutual ditch company shares are personal property (stock), so they transfer by stock assignment and a new certificate from the company. Other water rights are conveyed with the same formalities as real estate, usually by recorded deed.

questions.stem: A buyer plans to water a large lawn and garden at a home served by a household-use-only exempt well. What should the broker tell the buyer?
choices: The permit allows lawn and garden watering up to one acre
Use is limited to indoors in one home; no outside watering
Exempt wells have no use limits once ownership changes
The buyer may water outside if the assessor approves
questions.explanation: A household-use-only permit generally covers indoor use in one home with no outside watering, and a buyer must stay within the permit's limits. Up to one acre of lawn and garden goes with a domestic and livestock well, usually on 35+ acres.

questions.stem: A Colorado homeowner believes the county set the home's actual value too high. Where does the owner file the first protest?
choices: With the county assessor
With the county board of equalization
With the Board of Assessment Appeals
With the county treasurer
questions.explanation: A value protest goes to the assessor first, then the county board of equalization, then the Board of Assessment Appeals, district court or arbitration.

questions.stem: A U.S. citizen who lives in Texas sells a Colorado rental house for $300,000 and signs no exemption affirmation. Which withholding applies at closing?
choices: Both FIRPTA and Colorado withholding
FIRPTA withholding only
Colorado nonresident withholding only
Neither, because the seller is a U.S. citizen
questions.explanation: Colorado withholding turns on Colorado residency, and a Texas resident is a nonresident. FIRPTA turns on foreign status, so it doesn't apply to a U.S. citizen.

questions.stem: A renter believes a landlord discriminated against him because of his sexual orientation. Within what time may he file a charge with the Colorado Civil Rights Division?
choices: Within 60 days
Within 180 days
Within two years
Within one year
questions.explanation: A charge with the CCRD may be filed within one year of the discriminatory act. Two years is the time for a private lawsuit, not the CCRD charge.

questions.stem: Which landlord is exempt from Colorado's source-of-income provisions?
choices: A landlord who owns three rental units
A landlord who checks credit only for voucher holders
A landlord whose units are all single-family homes
A landlord who owns ten rental units but self-manages
questions.explanation: Landlords with three or fewer rental units are exempt from the source-of-income provisions. A covered landlord may check credit only if it checks every prospective tenant, not just voucher holders.

questions.stem: After a public trustee foreclosure sale of her home, the former owner asks how long she has to redeem. What is accurate under current Colorado law?
choices: She has 75 days after the sale to redeem
She has no right to redeem after the sale
She may redeem until the confirmation deed is recorded
She has 8 business days to file a notice of intent to redeem
questions.explanation: The owner has no post-sale right of redemption in Colorado. Redemption belongs to junior lienors whose liens were recorded before the notice of election and demand, and they file notice within 8 business days.

questions.stem: In a typical Colorado foreclosure of a home loan, who serves as trustee under the deed of trust?
choices: A private trust company chosen by the lender
The county sheriff
The county public trustee
The lender's attorney
questions.explanation: In Colorado, the trustee under a deed of trust is a government official, the county public trustee, who conducts most foreclosures as non-judicial sales. Sheriff's sales occur only in the less common court foreclosures.

questions.stem: A foreclosure consultant agrees to negotiate a forbearance for a homeowner. Under the Colorado Foreclosure Protection Act, when may the consultant collect a fee?
choices: When the homeowner signs the written contract
After fully performing every promised service
After securing the fee with a lien on the home
Once the lender acknowledges receiving the request
questions.explanation: A foreclosure consultant may not collect any fee until every promised service has been fully performed, and may not take a lien or wage assignment to secure the fee.

questions.stem: A licensed broker lists for sale the home of an owner who is behind on the mortgage and facing foreclosure. Is the broker a foreclosure consultant under the CFPA?
choices: Yes, because the owner's loan is delinquent
Yes, unless the broker charges no commission
No, as long as the broker acts within the license
No, but only if the sale is a short sale
questions.explanation: A licensed real estate broker acting within the license, such as by listing the home for sale, is excluded from the definition of a foreclosure consultant.

cards.back: Real estate = land plus permanent improvements. Real property = real estate plus the bundle of legal rights of ownership.
Possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, and disposition.
By a bill of sale, not a deed.
Method of attachment, Adaptability, Relationship of parties, Intention, Agreement. A written agreement overrides the others; intention is the key test.
Business equipment a tenant installs. It stays the tenant's personal property and must be removed before the lease ends.
Annual crops planted by labor. They're personal property; a tenant farmer may return to harvest them after the lease ends.
A right or improvement that runs with the land and passes with the deed, such as an easement appurtenant.
Riparian: owners along rivers and streams. Littoral: owners along lakes and oceans.
Water rights go to the first to put water to beneficial use ("first in time, first in right"). Colorado uses this system.
Describes a parcel by distances and directions from a point of beginning; it must return to the POB. Monuments generally control over distances.
Legal description by reference to a recorded subdivision plat.
6 miles × 6 miles = 36 square miles = 36 sections.
1 mile × 1 mile = 1 square mile = 640 acres.
Section 1: northeast corner of the township. Section 36: southeast corner.

cards.front: Acreage of the N 1/2 of the SW 1/4 of a section
Fee simple determinable vs. condition subsequent
cards.back: "So long as" = determinable, reverts automatically (possibility of reverter). "On condition that" = grantor must act (right of reentry).
A life estate measured by the life of someone other than the life tenant.
Remainder: goes to a named third party when a life estate ends. Reversion: goes back to the grantor or grantor's heirs.
Damage or neglect by a life tenant that lowers the property's value for the future owner. It isn't allowed.
Estate for years, periodic tenancy, tenancy at will, tenancy at sufferance.
Ownership by one person or one entity.
Possession, Interest, Time, Title (PITT).

cards.front: Effect of a joint tenant selling their share
cards.back: The buyer becomes a tenant in common; the remaining owners stay joint tenants with each other.

cards.front: Colorado presumption for conveyance to two or more people
cards.back: Tenancy in common, unless the deed expressly declares a joint tenancy (C.R.S. 38-31-101).

cards.front: Does Colorado recognize tenancy by the entirety?
cards.back: No. C.R.S. 38-31-201: an attempted tenancy by the entirety creates a joint tenancy.

cards.front: Is Colorado a community property state?
cards.back: No. Colorado divides marital property by equitable distribution.
Fee title to the unit plus an undivided interest as tenant in common in the common elements.
Shares in a corporation that owns the building plus a proprietary lease; usually treated as personal property.
Property tax and special assessment liens generally come before all other liens, whatever their recording date.
Appurtenant: has dominant and servient parcels and runs with the land. In gross: benefits a person or company and has no dominant parcel.
Merger, release, abandonment, end of necessity or purpose, and (in some states) non-use of a prescriptive easement.

Open, notorious, continuous, exclusive, hostile (adverse) for the statutory period. Colorado: 18 years (C.R.S. 38-41-101), plus clear and convincing proof and a good-faith belief of ownership for claims filed since July 1, 2008.
Government powers: Police power, Eminent domain, Taxation, Escheat.
Public use and just compensation. The legal process is condemnation.
A suit by an owner seeking compensation when government action has effectively taken or damaged the property.
A use that was legal before the current zoning; it's grandfathered but usually can't be expanded or rebuilt after destruction.
Relief from strict zoning requirements (setback, height) because of a hardship unique to the property.
Allows a use the ordinance permits under conditions, such as a church or school in a residential zone.
Rezoning one parcel inconsistently with the comprehensive plan to benefit one owner; often illegal.
Issued after final inspection; allows a building to be legally occupied.
The more restrictive rule generally governs.
Writing, competent grantor, identifiable grantee, consideration recital, granting clause, legal description, grantor's signature, delivery and acceptance.
General: warrants against defects from any time. Special: only defects arising during the grantor's ownership.
No warranties; conveys whatever interest the grantor has, if any. Used to clear clouds on title.
A later buyer wins only if they had no notice AND recorded first. Colorado's statute (C.R.S. 38-35-109) is race-notice.
Survey and inspection matters: encroachments, boundary disputes, parties in possession, unrecorded easements and mechanic's liens.
Owner's: protects the buyer, usually for the price, lasts while the owner or heirs hold an interest. Lender's: protects the lender for the loan amount.

cards.front: Equity of redemption vs. statutory redemption
cards.back: Equity: pay off and stop foreclosure before the sale. Statutory: buy back after the sale, where state law allows.
Testate: dies with a will (devise). Intestate: dies without a will (descent under state statute); no heirs = escheat.
Value = estimated worth to typical buyers; price = what was actually paid; cost = what it took to build.
Demand (with purchasing power), Utility, Scarcity, Transferability.
A buyer won't pay more than the cost of an equally desirable substitute. Basis of the sales comparison approach.

cards.front: Highest and best use: four tests
cards.back: Legally permissible, physically possible, financially feasible, maximally productive.
A component is worth what it adds to value, not what it cost.
Regression: best house on a modest street loses value. Progression: modest house among nicer homes gains value.
Value = present worth of expected future benefits. Drives the income approach.
Adjust the comp, never the subject. Comp better → subtract; comp worse → add.
Land value + (cost new − accrued depreciation).
Reproduction = exact replica, same materials. Replacement = same utility, modern materials.
Physical deterioration, functional obsolescence, external (economic) obsolescence.
External (economic) obsolescence — the cause is off the property.
No. Only improvements depreciate.
PGI − vacancy/collection loss = EGI; EGI − operating expenses = NOI; NOI ÷ cap rate = value.
Debt service (mortgage P&I) and the owner's income tax depreciation.
GRM = price ÷ monthly gross rent (1–4 units). GIM = price ÷ annual gross income (larger/commercial).

cards.front: Best approach for a church or fire station
cards.back: Cost approach — special-purpose property with few sales and no rental income.
Weighing the approaches to reach one final value opinion — not a simple average.
CMA/BPO = broker's market estimate. Appraisal = credentialed appraiser's formal opinion. Never call a CMA an appraisal.
Automated valuation model: software estimate from data, no inspection. Weak where sales are sparse.
Note = the debt (promise to pay). Mortgage/deed of trust = pledges property as collateral (lien).

cards.front: Parties to a deed of trust
cards.back: Trustor (borrower), beneficiary (lender), trustee. In Colorado, the trustee is usually the county public trustee.
Mortgagor = borrower (gives the mortgage). Mortgagee = lender.
Lien: borrower holds title, lender has a lien. Title: title conveyed to lender/trustee until paid.
On default, lender can declare the entire balance due.
Lender can call the loan if the property is transferred; blocks unapproved assumption.
Lender must release the lien when the debt is paid in full.
Subordination: lien agrees to rank behind a later lien. Release: frees parcels from a blanket loan as they're paid off.
Assumption: buyer becomes personally liable. Subject to: buyer pays but isn't personally liable.
1% of the loan amount (not the price). Prepaid interest to lower the rate.
Loan ÷ lesser of price or appraised value.
The lender, on a conventional loan with a small down payment (classically LTV above 80%).
Principal, interest, taxes, insurance — the full monthly housing payment.
Housing (front-end) = housing payment ÷ gross monthly income. Total (back-end) = housing + other debts ÷ gross monthly income.
Index = market rate, changes. Margin = lender markup, fixed. Rate = index + margin, limited by caps.
Payments don't cover interest, so unpaid interest is added and the balance grows.
FHA insures (mortgage insurance premiums). VA guarantees (no monthly MI; funding fee; eligibility certificate).
Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy loans. Ginnie Mae (in HUD) guarantees securities of government-backed loans; doesn't buy loans.
Seller keeps legal title until paid; buyer has possession and equitable title.
For older owners with equity; lender pays owner, balance grows; repaid on sale, permanent move-out or death.
No kickbacks, referral fees or unearned fee splits for settlement services on covered loans.
Written disclosure at or before referral; consumer not required to use affiliate; only return on ownership received.
Down payment amount/%, number of payments or term, payment amount, finance charge amount.
Delivered or mailed no later than the 3rd business day after the lender receives the application.
Consumer must receive it at least 3 business days before consummation.

cards.front: Changes that restart the 3-day CD wait
cards.back: APR becomes inaccurate, loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added.
Name, income, SSN (for credit report), property address, estimated value, loan amount sought.
Race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, public-assistance income, exercise of consumer credit rights.
3 business days on certain refinances/home-equity loans on a principal residence; not for purchase loans.
1 acre = 43,560 sq ft. 1 section = 640 acres = 1 sq mile.
Part = Whole × Rate; Rate = Part ÷ Whole; Whole = Part ÷ Rate.

cards.front: Price needed for a desired net
cards.back: (Desired net + dollar costs) ÷ (1 − commission rate).
360: every month = 30 days (annual ÷ 360). 365: actual days (annual ÷ 365).

cards.front: Taxes paid in arrears at closing
cards.back: Debit seller, credit buyer for the seller's share.
Income = Rate × Value. Cap rate = NOI ÷ value; value = NOI ÷ cap rate.
1 mill = $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. Tax = assessed value × mills ÷ 1,000.

cards.front: Monthly interest on an amortized loan
cards.back: Balance × annual rate ÷ 12. Payment − interest = principal reduction.
Market value − all loan balances.
Original = current ÷ (1 − loss rate). $180,000 after a 10% loss → $200,000.
Basis = original cost (plus certain acquisition costs). Adjusted basis = basis + capital improvements − depreciation and casualty losses.
Gain = Amount realized (price − selling costs) − Adjusted basis.
No. Only capital improvements (adding value or extending life) increase basis; ordinary repairs don't.

cards.front: Does the mortgage payoff affect taxable gain?
cards.back: No. Gain depends on amount realized and adjusted basis, not the loan balance.
Held one year or less = short-term (ordinary income rates). Held more than one year = long-term (lower rates).
Up to $250,000 single; up to $500,000 married filing jointly.

cards.front: Home-sale exclusion: ownership and use test
cards.back: Owned and lived in as a main home at least 2 of the 5 years before sale. Years needn't be consecutive.

cards.front: How often can the home-sale exclusion be used?
cards.back: Generally not if used on another home within the past 2 years; no lifetime limit.

cards.front: Loss on sale of your own home — deductible?
cards.back: No. Losses on personal-use property aren't deductible.

cards.front: Mortgage interest and property tax deductions
cards.back: Deductible only if the homeowner itemizes; dollar limits/caps are set by Congress and change.
No. Only buildings and other improvements can be depreciated.
27.5 years, straight-line.
39 years, straight-line.
(Cost − land value) ÷ 27.5 (residential rental) or ÷ 39 (nonresidential).
Depreciation lowers basis, increasing gain at sale; the depreciation portion of the gain is taxed under separate rules (often a higher rate). Depreciation defers tax, it doesn't erase it.
Real property held for investment or business use, exchanged for other such real property. Not a primary residence, a personally used vacation home, or property held for sale.
45 days to identify replacement property in writing; 180 days (or return due date incl. extensions, if earlier) to acquire it. Both run from the sale.
